There are two facts about this game. 1) You are a pug. 2) You were born to run. Except sometimes you're a cat or maybe a penguin. But mostly, you're a pug, and you run. You run through day. You run through night. You run through snow. You run through rain (and get electrocuted for your folly.) There are spikes and buzzsaws and lava in your way. There are also treasure chests. You ignore them. You are a pug. You have no thumbs and are too busy running.

You run, you jump over things, you collect coins and then you die. It's a pretty standard runner. But this one has pugs! Should you buy a game just because you control a pug? I think the answer is yes. 

There are weather changes as you play. Poor weather makes it harder to spot obstacles and getting hit by lighting will cause your pug to freeze for a second (even in the air). There are characters with different abilities (not many). I prefer to play as a pug because the cats sound so sad when they die and to me the pug's dying bark sounds of determination to get back out there and try again, which is also what I want to do.

The graphics and music are very nice. There's no controller support but the game only uses one button. There's not a lot of depth to the game but like any runner you just want to keep trying to beat your high score. The leaderboard unfortunately only shows the first ten names so you can't see what place you're in, and you can't view just your friends scores either which would be nice.

Overall I've found Turbo Pug to be a satisfactorily puggy game and I give it 10 tummy rubs.

Turbo Pug....how does one describe such a beauty in words? From the charming, relatable pugs & other animals found in Turbo Pug, to the inspiring virtual barks littered throughout the game's gorgeous soundtrack, Turbo Pug attempts what no game has done before, and vastly succeeds. A true revolution in the gaming industry, Turbo Pug not only offers a sense of realism, as the impeccable storytelling of the pug's life, including his mental and physical struggles (i.e. lightning) and his complex love life with Space Kitty offer a narrative never before seen. The game, or, masterpiece, also offers a style of gameplay entirely new to the industry, shaking up the game and acting as a message for triple A developers to step it up. There is a common question asked when dealing with video games... "are video games considered art?" Turbo Pug puts an end to this debate, silencing the haters, as there is no doubt in anyone's mind that this game is on par with the Mona Lisa. Turbo Pug deserves a standing ovation, in all honesty.
